741-elective-courses-15-24-credits: Any 200–500; a minor in another faculty may be possible with the Adviser.
741-program-description: For strong students heading to graduate school, with advanced courses and a final-year research project. 90 credits (120 with Foundation). CGPA 3.3 after two years, kept to graduation.
743-about-the-faculty-of-engineering: Since 1855, one of the world's leading engineering and design communities, with about 3,500 undergraduates and 1,200 graduate students, across engineering, architecture and urban planning. Internships, co-ops, design teams and research build real-world skills.
743-our-values: Sustainable excellence, open by design, equity embedded, creative exploration, and shared responsibility.
Accredited professional bachelor's degrees in all departments, and a non-professional degree in Architecture. The new B.G.E. isn't accredited yet.

Required courses build core principles, and complementaries let you specialize. Internship Program: 4–16 paid months. Co-ops in Mining, Materials and Software. Master's and doctorates across departments, with professional master's in Architecture and Urban Planning.
743-location: Dean's Office: Macdonald Engineering Building, 817 Sherbrooke St. W. McGill Engineering Student Centre (advising, tutoring, careers): Adams Building, 3450 University St., Suite 22.
744-bachelor-of-science-architecture: The first professional degree is the M.Arch. (Professional).
744-bachelor-of-engineering: CEAB-accredited, meeting academic requirements for provincial engineering bodies, with international agreements.

To be an engineer: pass an exam on law and practice, and get two to four years' experience. Only registered persons may use the title. In Québec, that's the OIQ, with McGill seminars and a student section. The B.G.E. isn't accredited.
744-admission-requirements: B.Eng., B.G.E. and B.Sc.(Arch.), with limited enrolment. See the Admissions guide.
744-student-activities: All undergraduates belong to the Engineering Undergraduate Society, which runs activities and clubs. Each department has an association, plus design teams.
744-student-progress: Finish within six years, usually less with Advanced Standing. The Committee on Standing may extend for serious medical or other uncontrollable reasons, or internships.
744-minors: Aerospace, Applied AI, Arts, Biomedical, Biotechnology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Construction, Economics, Environment, Environmental Engineering, Management (Finance, Management, Marketing, Operations), Materials, Mathematics, Mining, Musical Science and Technology, Nanotechnology, Physics, Software, and Technological Entrepreneurship.
745-engineering-internship-program: For full-time students in non-co-op degrees, giving formal recognition, which many employers require.
745-eligibility-criteria: Full-time before and after, 4, 8, 12 or 16 months at 35+ hours a week, paid, related to your degree. International students need a co-op permit. At most two academic terms missed. Possibly one course up to 4 credits meanwhile.
746-about-the-peter-guo-hua-fu-school-of: Founded in 1896. B.Sc.(Arch.), M.Arch. (Professional), M.Sc. in Architecture and Ph.D.
746-vision: Professional education through research, critical practice and community engagement.
746-mission: Educates professionals in designing, building and interpreting the built environment, with diverse teaching and research, multidisciplinary links, civic engagement and global exchange.
746-architectural-certification-in-canad: The M.Arch. is accredited by CACB, the sole Canadian authority, and recognized by NCARB in the U.S.
746-programs-of-study: For the professional degree, complete the B.Sc.(Arch.) with CGPA 3.00, which doesn't guarantee entry, and a portfolio from six design studios plus other work.
746-laboratories-and-workshops: Media Centre: Juan Osorio. Workshops: Athanasia Blounas, David Speller.
746-library: Blackader-Lauterman Collection, Redpath Library. Liaison: David Greene.
746-collections: John Bland Canadian Architecture Collection. Jennifer Garland, Rare Books.
746-location: Macdonald-Harrington Building, Room 201, 815 Sherbrooke St. W.
746-program-description: Foundations for the M.Arch. A first year of general studies (usually credited from a DCS), then six terms of studio on design, representation, construction and human experience, with lectures, complementaries and electives.
747-required-year-0-courses-28-credits: Usually credited from CEGEP; choose with the Student Advisor. 10 credits from the list (a mechanics PHYS may substitute). 3 credits at 100–200 in ATOC, COMP, ENVR or EPSC. 15 at 100–200 in humanities and social science subjects.
747-architectural-courses: ARCH 250 and 378 in your first year.
749-about-the-department-of-bioengineeri: Founded in 2012, undergraduate since Fall 2016. Streams: Biological Materials and Mechanics, Biomolecular and Cellular Engineering, Biological Information and Computation.
749-location: McConnell Engineering Building, Room 350, 3480 University St.
749-program-description: Applies biology, physical sciences, math and engineering to biological problems, both biological and biomedical engineering, with one specialization.
749-required-year-0-courses-29-credits: CEGEP usually gives credit except BIOL 112, available by passing the Science Placement Exam.
749-required-non-departmental-courses-27: CHEM 212 credit through the Placement Exam before your first term; otherwise take it here.
750-bioengineering-technical-courses-24-: From Year 2, take 30–31 credits, with required Technical Complementaries in one stream.
750-bioengineering-general-technical-cou: 9–10 credits. CHEE 563 or MECH 563; only one 4-credit course; at most 6 SEAD.
751-group-a-impact-of-technology-on-soci: 3 credits. Some need permission; prerequisites are strict. ENVR and Management courses have limits.
752-group-b-humanities-and-social-scienc: 6 credits; CEGEP usually gives 3. Arts courses at 200–300 in listed departments, not seminars, field, survey or topics courses or those with science or math content, or from listed Management, Science and Engineering courses. Reserved courses are restricted. INTG 215 isn't open after INTG 201 and 202.
753-about-the-department-of-chemical-eng: Physics, math and chemistry, with biology for bioprocessing, food and environment, plus design, economics and teamwork.

Graduates work in chemicals, energy, water, food and pharma, and the training suits environmental problems and further study like business, medicine or law. Minors in biotechnology, nanotechnology, management, materials and more.
753-academic-programs: 143 credits, 114 with CEGEP Pure and Applied Sciences. C or better in core courses, including technical complementaries.
753-canadian-society-for-chemical-engine: The student society is affiliated with CSChE, free for undergraduates, and AIChE, with member rates and events with the Montréal CIC section.
753-more-about-b-eng-degree-in-chemical-: Sequences: Polymers (CHEE 582, 584) and Materials (380, 384); Biotechnology (370, 474); Energy (400, 401, 511, 541); Pollution Control (521, 591, 593). A Biotechnology minor (p. 808).
Many complementaries run in alternate years, so plan ahead. Graduate CHEE courses are possible with approval.
754-location: M.H. Wong Building, Room 3060, 3610 University St.
754-program-description: Based on physics, math and chemistry, with biology, operations and economics, ending in design courses by practising engineers. Some finish in three calendar years with Summer, or two and a half from science. C or better in core.
754-note-to-cegep-students: Pass the Science Placement Exam for CHEM 212 or 234 credit, in August or September, with a fee. Otherwise take them here.
754-required-year-0-courses-26-credits: CEGEP usually gives credit. See the page for French and IB, AP and A-Levels.
755-list-a: 3–9 credits. CHEE 521 or CIVE 521; CHEE 563 or MECH 563; CHEE 593 or CIVE 430.
755-list-b: 0–6 credits, and only one project course: CHEE 494, 495 or 496.
756-list-c: 0–3 from other Engineering courses, with permission.
756-faculty-of-arts: 200–300 in listed departments, not seminars, field, survey or topics courses, or reserved ones, with some exclusions; or from listed Management, Science and Engineering courses. INTG 215 isn't open after INTG 201 and 202.
758-about-the-department-of-civil-engine: The built environment: buildings, bridges, roads, dams, water and transportation, with growing roles in rehabilitation and pollution prevention. Minors include Arts, Economics, Management, Environmental, and Construction.
758-academic-programs: Much freedom, with advanced courses in Environmental, Geotechnical, Water Resources, Structural and Transportation Engineering. A sample program guides you. See an adviser each term, and for transfers.
758-location: Macdonald Engineering Building, Room 495, 817 Sherbrooke St. W.
758-program-description: Mechanics and engineering fundamentals with specialization and modern tools. Required courses cover solids, fluids, soils, environment, water, structures, systems and math. Complementaries go deep or broad.
759-list-b-general-technical-complementa: 0–9 from the list or suitable others. CHEE 521 or CIVE 521.
